And morning overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent.

<center>The One Thousand and Seventh Night</center>

When the next night arrived, she said, "O auspicious King, the Queen said to the King, 'O my cousin, do not think that you love me, for I have attained your companionship.' When he heard her words and she was drunk, there was hidden in his soul what she had prepared for him. She tempted him and showed him love, and she slept beside him. When it was midnight, he rose from the bed, and King Badr was aware of her, but he pretended to be asleep. He opened one eye to see what she was doing. He found that she had taken out a bag of red earth and spread it in the middle of the palace. It became a flowing river. She took a handful of barley and scattered it on the earth, watering it with that water, so it became crops just as she had taken it. She harvested it and ground it, and it became flour. Then she asked him, and she came to the side and slept until morning. When morning came, King Badr got up and did his best to get permission from the Queen to go to the Elder. She gave him permission, so he went to the Elder and told him what he had seen from her. When the Elder heard that, he laughed and said, 'She has betrayed you, by God, this infidel, but do not honor her.' Then he brought him a pound of flour and said, 'Take this with you. When you come to her and she sees this flour with you and asks where you are going, say, "Adding good to good." Eat from it, and if she eats from it, she will offer you her flour, and if she tells you to eat of this flour, show her that you have eaten of it. Eat from this, but do not eat anything of her flour, for if she wants you to, she will deceive you. If she is convinced that you have eaten of her flour, she will move and tell you to "Exit from the natural form to the form you want." She will do the work if you eat from her flour, and if you do not eat, she will not think of you. Her magic will reveal the truth as it really is for you, and she will say to you, "I have returned...""

Lord Nabeshima Heizaemon-no-jō Kiyohisa resided in Honjō Village. Before the local festival, he and his wife would come out every night carrying poles, spending the entire night poking at the moat. Because people would drain the moat and catch carp for the festival, he did this to make the fish flee. Beyond that, his compassion regarding public works was boundless. In his daily life, he was a devout believer in the Hikosan faith, and every year at the year’s end, he would seclude himself in prayer. Once, while he was at the Upper Shrine, heavy snow fell and the path became unclear; he fell off a cliff and dropped into a valley. When they searched for him in that area, they found the <term>Amida Sanzon</term> <gloss>The Trinity of Amida Buddha</gloss> that he had been holding. He brought them back and made them the principal objects of worship for the Tokuzen Hikosan shrine. It is said that the original deity of Hikosan is the Amida Trinity. It is a mysterious event. It appears that the prosperity of his house is due to that merit. This is the rumor among the old folks.

The image of the Tokuzen Gongen deity is said to be the same as the principal image of the Zōryū-bō of Hikosan. It is said that when it was lost in a fire, the original image was sunk into a well, and because of that, the mountain was safe. I heard this story from the abbot some years ago. (The sacred body of Tokuzen Gongen is viewed during each succession.)

When Nabeshima Monda-dono was young, he was taken in as an adopted son by Lord Naoshige. However, upon the birth of Lord Katsushige, the fief at the former site of Yokotake was given to Monda-dono.

...to do evil to him for good, according to the thought and intention they have at the time of their contemplation and their desire to influence that matter with good or evil. With this, the cause of the matter of amulets and incantations will be clarified, and the benefit drawn from them according to the mentioning of a thing without contemplation. It acts like the specific magic in a specific Kabbalah from it, the content of a seal of a property <note>term: "segulah"</note> and its cause. This is not understood. 

From this matter, as it is said in the words of our Sages in tractate *Shabbat*, in the chapter "Those who whisper" <note>term: "Lachashin"</note>. Three of wisdom are hinted at here. They act in matters of the selection of the Sages. For their mouth is the body, and this is the cause of the property of the seal of the incantations. Because the incantation placed in their mouth was useful, as it is said: "Life is in the hand of the tongue." Assistance will not be supported by the seal of the incantation written by those who whisper, but by the seal of the incantations of others according to the degree of their perfection with them, of blessed memory. The absence of the seal of the property from the seal of the Sages is because it moved from their mouths. They say "from the mouth of those who whisper," as it was noted what acquired a certain property. When it is moved from its place, its property is lost. 

Therefore, any matter that was once a source of properties for medicines for the doctors of their time, they established a seal and wrote it in a book. In our time, their property is absent because of the transfer of the seal from place to place. There is no doubt that the place has a great impression on the acquisition of the property or the form for a matter. As mentioned in the fourth book of the *Sefer Ha-Kilyot* <gloss>Book of Kidneys</gloss>. If so, the action of the names and the amulets is in the Kabbalah. It is possible that the seal of the property is absent when transferring things from mouth to mouth. 

As the Sages said: "For the correction of those who whisper, they do not act by themselves but only for the seal from the absolute mouth." Behold, the whisper before eating kills the scorpion, etc. It is said that the whisper depends on the person <note>term: "chomet"</note> according to his level and his place in wisdom. His words will act on things that stand outside, as explained regarding the prophets. According to their perfection in it, they produced signs. Until there was one whose speech acts and makes an impression on the celestial bodies, as the sun stood in Gibeon, and it is written: "And the sun stood still," etc. Among the Sages of Egypt, they would act by the gaze of their eyes, as it is said: "He cast his eyes upon him and he became a heap of bones." 

One should not wonder at this, for it is found in the nature of animals that one kills by the sight of its eye. Why should it be unique to the nature of a person's temperament? So too if the eyes of a holy one are focused, they will harm the wicked and do good for the righteous. It is within the power of the sight and the line of sight that goes out from it to everything that receives the influence. Since the essence of wisdom is recognized by the depth of contemplation and the gaze of its vision, they are like arrows in the hand of a warrior. 

As our Sages said regarding the approach of the person, the son of Judah, the son of Gerim, and many like these. So if a physical human speech is found to have a small action, how much more so for a spiritual person. If a spiritual intellectual speech is found, it will produce comprehensive actions and deeds. From this matter and kind is the "by the word of the Lord the heavens were made." So too with the prophets and the amulet. Before he speaks, the word of the Lord is on his mouth. This speech is according to the level of the speaker and his closeness to his Creator. So too says the wise man mentioned in the book *Or Ha-Sekhel* <gloss>Light of the Intellect</gloss>: "Thus the Divine speech looks to everyone who speaks it, or speaks to him, and will speak in the future." 

This is the concept of "and he was silenced with the name of speech," because speech indicates leadership, from the translation "and he shall lead" <note>term: "ve-dibber"</note>. There is an ultimate distinction between them in essence and matter, except for the name of the intention and what it indicates. The strength of the name being this speech is filled with the completion of desire, intention, and will. This is also in its image. Understand this well from the truth. Behold, you are a source of rising in particular matters. This is my opinion on this matter. It is a place for everyone according to their knowledge.

For many and great things were done and spoken each day by the Goddess toward him, which, since they are innumerable and unheard of, I myself do not now hold in precise memory. CHAPTER III.
*Examination of the State of a Woman's Mind*

WHEN a man is trying to gain over a woman he should examine the state of her mind, and act as follows.

If she listens to him, but does not manifest to him in any way her own intentions, he should then try to gain her over by means of a go-between.

If she meets him once, and again comes to meet him better dressed than before, or comes to him in some lonely place, he should be certain that she is capable of being enjoyed by the use of a little force. A woman who lets a man make up to her, but does not give herself up, even after a long time, should be considered as a trifler in love, but owing to the fickleness of the human mind, even such a woman can be conquered by always keeping up a close acquaintance with her.

They brought back a long report of the coast they saw, and some natives from those southern coasts also came in their company. The general <note>Hernando Cortés</note> received both the Spaniards and the natives graciously and informed them of the greatness and power of Their Majesties; he gave them some jewelry, with which they departed very content and astonished to see the horses, weapons, artillery, and the manner of the Spaniards.

At the time when the Indians defeated and drove Hernando Cortés and the Spaniards out of Temistitan <note>Tenochtitlán, the Aztec capital</note>, all the provinces subject to that great city rebelled. As it appears from the preceding chapters, all or most of that land was reconquered and subjugated by the industry, courage, and good diligence of the general—sometimes without shedding blood, and also with punishment and the sword where it was necessary to use arms. Because certain provinces, which are ten, fifteen, or thirty leagues from this North Sea of ours <note>The Atlantic/Gulf of Mexico</note>, had been in rebellion since the city had risen up, and their natives had treacherously and under a false sense of security killed more than one hundred Spaniards at various times, their punishment had been deferred until the conclusion of the war and the siege of the city; for before then, there was no possibility or means to attend to it. Thus, as soon as the general had dispatched the aforementioned messengers to the South Sea <note>The Pacific Ocean</note>, he immediately arranged to send the Chief Constable <term>alguaçil mayor</term> <note>a high-ranking officer responsible for justice and military discipline</note> Gonzalo de Sandoval with thirty-five horsemen and two hundred Spaniards, along with some allied people and several lords and natives of Temistitan to those provinces. This was so they might better understand, as eyewitnesses, what had been done and punished, for two reasons: the first,

The very study of gold-making <term>Chrysopoeia</term> <note>The art of transmuting base metals into gold.</note> is such that, according to the testimony of Delrio and Valencia <note>Martin Delrio (1551–1608) and Gregory of Valencia (1549–1603), Jesuit theologians who wrote on magic and moral philosophy.</note>, it hardly escapes the fault of vanity, while he who seeks profit from it does not easily escape the mark of imprudence. For is a merchant of sound mind who applies himself to that kind of business in which he sees none—or perhaps one out of several thousand—has made gold, while all others, or a thousand against one, have consumed their resources? Since this happens to students of the gold-making art, they are deservedly, to put it most mildly, accused of simplicity. If Nature is difficult, one easily descends to seeking the help of the Demon through the hope of gaining wealth from meager means. For whenever Alchemy flourished among many, according to Delrio, then Sorcery and Divination also flourished; a loss of most precious time is made, and an account of its evil consumption and never-to-be-redeemed status must be rendered to God.
